experiment: E-39c_pre: KL pre-gate + behavioral budget for M_K-surgery (round 2: tied-weight KL decomposition + α-blend sweep)
id_note: Renamed from exp39b_kl_surgery (ID collision with the real E-39b = PTQ/GPTQ gate, TЗ §2; see E39_fixes §0).

params.kl_pass_rationale: half of the E-16 KL leash (0.1)
params.gate_token_rule: t≥1 (round 2 §4.1: t=0 is the unconditioned first token, not a behavioral cost)

row_diag.space: W_lm (dW = M_kp/g − W_lm_old; ratios in W_lm-space)

kl_decomposition_tied_weights.note: 0.8B ties lm_head↔embed_tokens; the full edit changes both readout and input embeddings (→ all 24 layers). Three untied states split the cost. Values are mean KL over real tokens (t≥1). 'full' uses the RAW bottom-16 V_new (VU[:,-16:], orthogonalize=False) — NOT the orthogonalized blend endpoint, and NOT the E-39a a_random design (bottom-64 random; see v_new_strategy_sensitivity.strategies.a_random = 6.10). The headline full-surgery KL is the bottom-16 raw-rotation cost.
kl_decomposition_tied_weights.interpretation: head_only = readout-only cost; embed_only = upstream propagation; full ≈ head_only + embed_only + cross term (tied model). If embed_only dominates, the surgery is NOT readout-only: it edits the input embeddings, so the 'a flat leaf is cheap' claim is confounded by tied weights. (Round 2 §5.1: the decomposition exposes that the tied model has no cheap readout-only path.)

alpha_blend_sweep.construction: V_mixed(α)=√α·V_new_perp+√(1−α)·V_top (NO QR — orthonormal by construction since V_new_perp⊥V_top; round 3 §2.2 fix) where V_new_perp is V_new orthogonalized against V_top; M_kp(α)=U_top·Σ_top·V_mixed(α)ᵀ+M_rest; α=0 no-op, α=1 = V_new_perp endpoint. Per-column ‖V_mixed−V_top‖ = √(2−2√(1−α)) exactly (a clean rotation, not a sign-flip artifact).

blend_stability.overlap_note: ‖V_newᵀV_top‖_F: 0 = orthogonal, 4 = fully aligned. Here ~0.53 (modest, non-zero), so the raw V_new and V_top overlap; orthogonalizing to V_new_perp removes it and makes the blend a clean monotonic Grassmannian path.

blend_diagnostics.detail: round 3 §2.4: for a clean blend every column of V_mixed has per-column perturbation EXACTLY √(2−2√(1−α)) (uniform, min≈max≈expected). This verifies the blend is a true partial rotation. The EARLIER QR-blend version had per-column max ≈ 1.97 at α=0.1 (vs expected 0.32) — 7/16 columns sign-flipped by QR (Householder) and silently NEGATED M_kp terms, which inflated the row change (0.77 vs 0.23) and made the KL spuriously non-monotonic. With the QR removed, the row change is monotone in α and the small-α point is a genuinely small rotation.

alpha_blend_sweep.endpoint_note: TWO distinct full-rotation values — cite the right one in the paper: (1) headline FULL surgery (bottom-16 RAW V_new = VU[:,-16:], orthogonalize=False) = kl_decomposition_tied_weights.full = 6.31; (2) the α-blend's ORTHOGONALIZED endpoint (V_new_perp = V_new minus its V_top component) at α=1 = points[α=1].kl_t1 = 6.73. Gap = +0.41 (6.5%): the orthogonalized endpoint is HIGHER than the raw bottom-16 rotation. Both are KL-infeasible. (The ACTUAL E-39a a_random design — bottom-64 random, not bottom-16 — costs 6.10; see v_new_strategy_sensitivity.)
alpha_blend_sweep.kappa_note: round 4 §6: κ'(α) IS measured per α (dry-run on the base-model û_t, E-39a's exact _kappa_dryrun, N=32). The round-2/3 claim 'the flattening side is already satisfied' was WRONG: E-39a's a_random κ' (post-fix: 0.000297, from the E-39a JSON) applies ONLY at α=1 (full rotation). At small α the top-16 subspace is dominated by V_top, so κ' stays near the base 0.0162. Hence the KL budget (KL<0.05, small α) and the flattening target (κ'<0.005, large α) are SIMULTANEOUSLY binding — see alpha_blend_sweep.trade_off.
alpha_blend_sweep.conclusion: on the tested grid (α ∈ [0.0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.08, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1.0], incl. α<0.1), NO α satisfies BOTH constraints. NO α passes the KL budget: min KL = 0.1347 at α=0.01 (2.69× over); at that α, κ'≈0.0157 (≃3× the 0.005 target). The κ' target is reached only at α ∈ [0.7, 0.9, 1.0], where KL = 6.29–6.75 (≃126–135× over). The two feasible regions are DISJOINT (trade_off) — the route is infeasible by TENSION, not a thin margin. The clean (QR-free) blend makes KL monotone in α, so this is not a blend artifact. Full surgery (α=1) is refuted on KL (~126× over).
alpha_blend_sweep.budget_note: NO α on the tested grid passes the KL budget: min KL = 0.1347 at α=0.01 (2.69× over). Since KL increases monotonically with α (clean_rotation_verified), no smaller α can help. The κ' target (<0.005) is reached only at α ∈ [0.7, 0.9, 1.0], where KL = 6.29–6.75 (126–135× over budget). The feasible regions are DISJOINT — the route is infeasible by tension, not by a thin margin. (At the smallest α, κ'≈0.0157 ≃3× the target; at the smallest κ'-passing α=0.7, KL≈6.29.)

v_new_strategy_sensitivity.note: E-39a's three V_new strategies in the bottom-64 pool, evaluated at full surgery (α=1). If NO direction is KL-safe, the surgery is infeasible regardless of the V_new choice — a stronger negative result.

e39a_consistency.note: a_random (E-39c_pre) vs a_random (E-39a) dry-run κ'. Small diff (≲1e-3) confirms the E-39c_pre V_new construction + _kappa_dryrun pipeline reproduce E-39a. (A larger diff would flag a construction/convention mismatch.)

v_new_strategy_sensitivity.conclusion: no V_new direction is KL-safe at full surgery — the failure is structural (no V_new in the bottom pool is KL-safe at full rotation), not a consequence of the bottom-16 choice; per-strategy κ' dry-run also reported (round 4)

kappa_dryrun_alpha1.note: round 4: per-α κ' DRY-RUN is now measured (base-model û_t, E-39a's exact _kappa_dryrun, N=32). Edited-model û_t differ due to tied weights — this is a DRY-RUN, NOT an E-39c measurement. See alpha_blend_sweep.points[].kappa_dryrun and .trade_off.

gate.metric: mean KL over real tokens, t≥1, padding excluded (round 2 §4.1)
gate.basis: KL only (κ' is a dry-run preview, not a gate input)

limitations: Tied weights: editing W_lm = editing embed_tokens — the forward changes beyond the readout (TЗ §3.5). round 2 §5.1 decomposes this into head_only vs embed_only; the FULL (real model) cost is the sum of both.
C4 disjointness: ds.skip(4096) vs the 27b cache's first docs — disjoint by offset, NOT hash-verified.
KL_PASS=0.05 is a protocol choice (half of E-16's 0.1 leash), not derived from data.
κ' is a dry-run preview on base-model û_t; the real E-39c measurement happens on the edited model.

α-blend V_new is the bottom-16 (E-39a 'a'-equivalent) subspace across the α grid; the three E-39a strategies are compared only at FULL surgery (round 2 §5.3), not across α. round 3 §2.2: the blend is orthogonalized (V_new_perp ⊥ V_top) AND the QR on the combo is removed (orthonormal by construction), so it is a verified clean partial rotation (per-column perturbation = √(2−2√(1−α)) exactly; see alpha_blend_sweep.blend_diagnostics). The earlier QR-blend's non-monotonicity was a Householder sign-flip artifact (silent negation of M_kp terms), not a loss-landscape property. The α=1 blend endpoint is V_new_perp, ≈ the full-surgery raw-V_new design (kl_decomposition_tied_weights); both are KL-infeasible.

Per-α κ' IS measured (round 4 §3) as a DRY-RUN on the base-model û_t (E-39a's _kappa_dryrun, N=32). This is a PREVIEW, not an E-39c measurement: the real edited-model κ'(α) could differ (tied weights). The trade-off verdict (KL budget vs flattening target across α) rests on this dry-run κ'(α); a real E-39c measurement at a candidate α would be needed to confirm.

κ' dry-run uses the 32-doc cache (N=32, S=128) — the SAME convention as E-39a (its a_random dry-run = 0.0040). The KL side uses only 8 fresh C4 docs (skip 4096), so KL and κ' are measured on different doc sets (both base-model references, disjoint from each other by offset). The a_random consistency check in v_new_strategy_sensitivity.e39a_consistency validates the pipeline.
